messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: billing-metering-emitter-delay (eu-west-1). Symptom: token emit batches are delayed ~3-12m; downstream recon reports late -> potential overage flags. Pager level: P2. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/metering-delay

alice: /accept — I'll take it, oncall here. Starting initial triage.

alice: quick health checks: Kinesis consumer group meter-emits-eu shows lag, redis emitter_kv_cache TTL backlog growing. Hoping this is consumer-side.

sam: looking at metrics now. kinesis_put_latency slightly elevated, but 90p spikes on emitter pods CPU at 85%.

jess: billing-eng joining. Do we see duplicated token counts or just delayed delivery? Need to know if customers will be charged twice.

alice: logs show repeated warnings, not obvious duplicates:
```
2024-03-15T08:45:12Z emitter[pid=2031] WARN emit_retry window_gap=00:00:09 batch_size=128 last_seq=49821
2024-03-15T08:45:18Z emitter[pid=2031] INFO enqueued 128 tokens for dispatch seq=49822
```
Looks like batch sizing backoff + consumer lag, not retransmit duplicates yet.

sam: I restarted the consumer process on eu-west-1 (deploy id: deploy-meter-20240315-12). Scaling emitter pods + bumped inflight to 200.

alice: after restart consumer lag down from ~12m -> ~1.2m within 2m. CPU on pods settling.

jess: I'll temporarily mute automated overage email rule for eu-west-1 (rule id: billing-overage-eu). We should avoid noisy customer alerts while counts reconcile. Will log action and re-enable once stable.

maria: Support here — prepping a proactive note for customers on affected plans. Short template ready, will hold until we confirm no billing spikes. cc: @jess for final wording.

leif: Product ops checking dashboards — could delayed emits produce brief spikes in customer dashboards when backlog flushes?

jess: Possibly a small short-lived uptick when the backlog empties. That's expected behavior if timestamps are delayed but counts are correct. We're not seeing duplicate seq ids in the short term.

alice: mitigation summary: consumer restart + emitter scale. Monitoring for duplicates and recon delta. Also enabled a short shadow write to backup-accumulator for forensic trace.

sam: running a quick sweep: grep for duplicate seq ids across last 6h; no hits so far. command used: `zgrep "seq=\d\+" /var/log/emitter/*.log | cut -d' ' -f6 | sort | uniq -d` (still running).

jess: I'm turning on a soft-hold in billing pipeline that suppresses immediate overage flag escalation for records with timestamps older than 15m to allow graceful reconciliation. Documented in runbook.

maria: queued initial support DM to 4 customers in the affected region that reported UI blips earlier. No paid accounts escalated yet.

alice: metrics check at 08:55 UTC: consumer lag ~45s, emit rate back to normal. No duplicate detection alerts.

incident-bot: Note: runbook step 4 (disable overage emails) executed by jess at 2024-03-15T08:53:10Z.

leif: recommended follow-ups: 1) postmortem root-cause analysis (who owns emitter backpressure tuning), 2) add alert for emitter batch_size backoff, 3) evaluate autoscale thresholds.

jess: agreed. I'll own the alert tuning and the soft-hold logic improvement.

alice: handing off monitoring to sam for the next 90m. I will create a Slack reminder and link to logs: https://logs.redwood/emitter/eu/1713054321.

sam: ack — I'll watch for any recon deltas or duplicate seq ids and escalate if anything deviates.

maria: support will wait to send broader customer comms until recon confirms no overcharges.

alice: final note before handoff: temporary mitigations in place, no confirmed customer overcharge, silenced overage emails for eu-west-1, backlog draining. Will open a follow-up incident ticket for RCA and capacity work. :white_check_mark:
